talks.title: (2024) - Closing & prize ceremonies
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of (2024) - Closing & prize ceremonies.
talks.summary:
Overview: CrikeyCon IX closing ceremony covers lockpicking competition results, CTF standings with 174 registered users and 85 teams, and volunteer recognition.

Key Topics: Lockpicking competition with Lego-based challenges; CTF with most challenges solved except lockpicking and ninja levels; trophy presentations; and volunteer team acknowledgments.

Technical Details: The CTF ran all day with 174 registered users across 85 teams. Only two challenges remained unsolved: lockpicking level 3 and a ninja level 4 challenge. Organizers humorously credit themselves for docker-compose up while volunteers did the real work.

Takeaways: Conference competitions build community engagement beyond talks. CTF design balancing accessibility with challenge ensures broad participation.

talks.summary:
Welcome to CrikeyCon IX

Organizers Wade and Glenn open the ninth Brisbane event with an Acknowledgement of Country for Turrbal and Yuggera peoples. They note the community skipped two pandemic years, making this the tenth anniversary season.

Community Growth and Charity

First CrikeyCon at the Polish Club had about sixty-eight attendees; recent events neared one thousand tickets. Surplus funds donate to local charities, totaling over $125,000 across causes such as indigenous literacy, homelessness, and women's shelters.

Audience and Format

Hands-up polls show many first-timers, interstate visitors, industry professionals, hobbyists, and newcomers. The conference avoids rigid tracks but adds workshops and longer sessions in adjacent rooms while keeping a single-stage main program.

Sponsors and Contributors

Platinum sponsors dotc and Queensland Government return, joined by long-time gold supporters including Securo, Versent, Databricks, Division5, and Sidearm. Organizers thank speakers, volunteers, and attendees because ticket revenue alone cannot fund the event.

talks.title: (2024) - Lynore Close - Not Your Average Cyber Strategy: Tying in Co-design
talks.teaser: Security researchers examine technical aspects of (2024) - Lynore Close - Not Your Average Cyber Strategy: Tying in Co-design.
talks.summary:
Why co-design matters

Lynore Close argues cybersecurity strategy must move beyond technical silos amid burnout, skills shortages, board communication gaps, and diversity challenges. Qualified talent often already exists outside security teams.

Co-design defined

Co-design is a collaborative, iterative, human-centric model pairing security with cyber-adjacent stakeholders to understand real problems, improve outcomes, and avoid token consultation. Principles include outcomes focus, inclusivity, participation, respect, and adaptability.

Change frameworks

She links co-design to social learning theory and Kotter's eight-step change model—urgency, coalition, vision, empowerment, quick wins, and sustaining change. Security wins by understanding why people work insecurely, building trust, and creating champions rather than dictating fixes.

talks.title: (2024) - Sebastien Macke - Keeping up with the Pwnses
talks.teaser: Presenters detail vulnerability discovery and exploitation in (2024) - Sebastien Macke - Keeping up with the Pwnses - A walk-through of Talkback.
talks.summary:
## The Infosec Firehose Problem

Sebastien Macke of L'atelier introduces Talkback, an internal tool built to tame security news overload. Before Talkback, the team relied on Twitter, Reddit, and chat, seeing the same links reposted endlessly while spending hours scrolling.

## How Talkback Works

Talkback ingests resources into a searchable database. Seeds come from Reddit, Twitter, and conference archives; it then discovers RSS feeds for high-value source sites and auto-subscribes when reputation scores justify tracking.

## Scoring and Curation

Each item gets a heat score based on social popularity and whether trusted curators previously featured the source domain. Simple rules flag news versus technical content, and separate menus let users focus on research write-ups instead of headlines.

## Open Sourcing the Approach

Macke shares the pipeline so others can replicate curated, deduplicated infosec reading lists. Talkback aims to make staying current efficient—surfacing signal once, ranking it, and reducing duplicate noise across platforms.
